acceptance_criteria_results.3_lt_960_panel_hidden_full_width: PASS — resized to 800x900: ProjectContextPanel is fully hidden (raised element not found via TreeWalker; screenshot confirms full-width single column). Bottom tab bar restored with 5 role='tab' bottom-nav entries + inner ProjectDetail tabs.
acceptance_criteria_results.4_wizard_prism_visual_language: PASS — /projects/create shows 'NEW PROJECT · STEP 1 OF 4' eyebrow (top-right), large serif 'Basics' heading (Instrument Serif), and 01/02/03/04 segmented pill StepIndicator with labels Basics/Details/Documents/Review beneath. acceptance_criteria_results.6_investor_desktop_rail_no_errors: PASS — investor@ribhshare.com signs in to /home, DesktopLeftRail shows Home / Portfolio / Statements / Notifications / Profile (Invitations & Explore hidden per visibility rules — investor has no active invites/explore access on seed). Home renders 'Good Afternoon, Investor' hero + Total Invested ₦0 + Portfolio/Invites/Statements/Activity quick-access tiles. /portfolio and /statements load without console errors. ZERO console errors captured across the Investor session.

critical_code_review_comments: ProjectContextPanel gates purely on Platform.OS==='web' && width>=960 via useProjectSplitLayout(). Consider adding a data-testid='project-context-panel' on the outermost <View> to make future Playwright assertions cheaper (currently the panel has no explicit testID — we relied on text-content anchors like 'RAISED' / 'UNIT REGISTER' / 'Stage' and their bounding rects).

CreateProjectWizard's Step 1 initial render shows red inline validation messages ('Name must be at least 2 characters', 'Sector is required', 'Location is required', 'Target must be greater than zero') BEFORE the user has interacted with any field. This is the standard react-hook-form 'mode: onTouched' vs 'onChange' vs 'onSubmit' choice — consider switching to onSubmit-only (or shouldShowError only after touch/dirty) so a first-time user isn't greeted with a wall of red on Step 1. Not a functional bug, but a UX first-impression issue for a Prism-grade product.
